answer.short: Vertical asymptotes: $x=-4,-2,2$. Horizontal asymptote: $y=0$. $y$-intercept: $(0,\tfrac14)$. No $x$-intercepts. The reciprocal has the same sign as $f(x)$.
answer.worked:
Map each point $(a,b)$ to $(a,\tfrac1b)$ where $b\ne0$. The zeros give vertical asymptotes $x=-4,-2,2$, and $f(0)=4$ gives the intercept $(0,\tfrac14)$. Preserve the sign of each branch.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac1{f(x)}&\to-\infty &&\text{as }x\to-4^-\text{ or }-4^+\\\frac1{f(x)}&\to-\infty &&\text{as }x\to-2^-\\\frac1{f(x)}&\to+\infty &&\text{as }x\to-2^+\\\frac1{f(x)}&\to+\infty &&\text{as }x\to2^-\text{ or }2^+\\\frac1{f(x)}&\to0^- &&\text{as }x\to-\infty\\\frac1{f(x)}&\to0^+ &&\text{as }x\to+\infty\end{aligned}$$

Points where $f(x)=1$ or $f(x)=-1$ remain unchanged. Map the nonzero turning points by the same reciprocal rule and reverse increasing/decreasing behaviour on each branch. Exclude $x=-4,-2,2$ from the domain.
